newsitem.title: USA: ABC mulls how far to take "Ellen".
newsitem.headline: ABC mulls how far to take "Ellen".

text.p: Now that they've brought her out of the closet, will ABC let the star of its TV sitcom "Ellen" actually have a sex life this season?

ABC Entertainment President Jamie Tarses told television writers Wednesday the network planned to move slowly in developing the Ellen character as an open lesbian. The series, which stars Ellen DeGeneres, won top ratings for an episode last season that showed the character coming to realize she was gay, but also received harsh criticism from large segments of the viewing public.

"Ellen will, at some point or another, be dating or pursuing relationships, but that is a bit down the line," Tarses said. "Our feeling is this is a realization that the character has just made, and now must explore making that decision."

ABC's "Ellen" was the first network television series to feature an openly gay main character. Despite that bold move, many people wonder whether ABC will follow through with a three-dimensional lesbian character who kisses and goes to bed with other women.
Other television series such as the Fox show "Melrose Place" have long featured gay minor characters, but have avoided heated controversy by denying those characters much of an on-air sex life.

Tarses said ABC's plans to move slowly with "Ellen" would be in keeping with the indecisive personality of the character, who she said has been shown in past seasons to "equivocate on any and all things."
"It's going to be about baby steps for this character to get comfortable with the decision she's made."
"Will we see any baby kisses?" a reported asked.
"You know, we haven't gotten that far down the line," Tarses responded.

ABC's decision to bring the Ellen character out of the closet was one of the main objections cited by the Southern Baptists for organizing a boycott of ABC's parent, Walt Disney Co. Other conservative Christian groups on Wednesday joined the Baptists in speaking out against what they called Disney's intolerance of family values.
